title: Supreme Courage 4
content:
Once he judged they’d put enough distance between themselves and the creature to be reasonably safe, Wei Wuxian wheeled around and set Lan Wangji down with the gentlest care he could muster.

Lan Wangji’s leg hadn’t even begun to knit together properly before taking the full brunt of the beast’s jaws and soaking in foul subterranean water. Beneath his torn white robes, the fabric bloomed with wide, vivid stains of crimson, punctuated by the unmistakable, mangled puncture wounds left by overlapping rows of fangs. The moment Wei Wuxian let go, Lan Wangji’s strength gave out entirely, collapsing him to the cold stone.

Wei Wuxian bent double to inspect the damage, then straightened back up to scout the hollows of the cave. Despite the subterranean gloom, scrubby brush managed to take root here and there. After turning over a few rocks, he unearthed a pair of reasonably thick, straight branches. Wiping the grime and loose dirt away with the hem of his sleeve, he dropped into a crouch before Lan Wangji.

"Got any cord or ties on you?" He paused, his gaze landing on the spotless silk across Lan Wangji’s brow. "Hey, your ribbon’s perfect. Come on, take it off."

Before Lan Wangji could so much as part his lips to object, Wei Wuxian’s hand whipped out—swift as a striking viper—and snatched the forehead ribbon clean off his brow. With a practiced snap of his wrists, he turned the sacred silk into a makeshift splint bandage, aligning Lan Wangji’s battered leg against the branches and binding it fast with ruthless precision.

Lan Wangji’s pale eyes blew wide in sheer, unadulterated disbelief. "You...!"

Wei Wuxian’s fingers flew, looping the knot tight before Lan Wangji could finish sputtering. Giving the man's shoulder an airy, consoling pat, he coaxed, "What 'you'? Look, don't sweat the small stuff right now. No matter how much you treasure this strip of silk, it's not worth your leg, is it?"

Lan Wangji slumped back against the rock face, eyes fluttering shut—whether because his remaining stamina had run dry or because he’d been rendered utterly speechless by the indignity, it was impossible to tell.

Just then, a faint whiff of dry, earthy fragrance teased Wei Wuxian’s nose. He reached into his lapel, his fingers brushing against silk, and pulled out a small sachet.

Its silken tassels hung sodden and limp, looking dainty yet pathetically drenched. Remembering Mianmian’s offhand comment that it was stuffed with crushed herbs, he tore the stitching open on the spot. Sure enough, tucked inside were handfuls of half-damp, coarsely ground medicinal leaves, mixed with a scattering of tiny, preserved blossoms.

He nudged Lan Wangji eagerly. "Lan Zhan, Lan Zhan, don’t pass out just yet! Sit up for a second. Look, I’ve got a medicine pouch here—take a look and see if there's anything we can actually use."

Through sheer, relentless pestering—tugging, dragging, and whining like an insufferable brat—he wore Lan Wangji down until the young master forced his heavy lids open and dragged himself upright. Lan Wangji cast a tired, analytical glance over the mess, his sharp eyes picking out several leaves known for stemming blood and neutralizing minor venoms.

Wei Wuxian sorted them out, chuckling, "Who would've thought that little lady's pouch would save our necks? I owe her big time once we get back."

Lan Wangji’s tone was deadpan. "You mean you intend to harass her properly."

"What's that supposed to mean?" Wei Wuxian scoffed playfully. "When I do it, it's charming banter. It only counts as harassment when it comes from a greasy toad like Wen Chao! Now, strip."

Lan Wangji’s brow pinched into a sharp furrow. "What?"

"What do you mean, 'what'? Take your clothes off!"

Before Lan Wangji could process the order, Wei Wuxian took matters into his own hands. Grabbing Lan Wangji by the collar with both fists, he yanked outward with decisive force, instantly laying bare a pristine expanse of pale chest and sculpted shoulders.

Pinned flat against the cold cavern floor, his robes ripped open by force, Lan Wangji’s face turned an apocalyptic shade of green. "Wei Ying! What do you think you are doing?!"

Wei Wuxian peeled the layers clean off him, tearing the fabric into long strips with clean, sharp rips. "What do I think I’m doing? We're alone in the dark, miles beneath the earth, and I've already stripped you down this far. Take a wild guess!"

With that, he rose to his feet, reached for his own sash, and loosened it in a display of mock courtesy—baring his own torso to the damp air.

His collarbones were deeply cast and fluidly sculpted, carrying the lean, spring-loaded vitality of youth, raw with wiry muscle and restless energy.

Lan Wangji stared at the spectacle before him, his complexion shifting violently through a kaleidoscope of pale white, bruised purple, and furious crimson. He looked on the absolute brink of coughing up a lungful of blood.

Wei Wuxian offered a roguish grin, closing the distance between them by a single, deliberate step. Right before Lan Wangji’s unblinking, mortified gaze, he shrugged off his sodden outer robe, gave it an airy snap in the air, and let it flutter carelessly to the stone floor.

Spreading his hands wide, Wei Wuxian declared, "Top’s off. Pants next!"

Lan Wangji tried to scramble to his feet, but his mangled leg betrayed him. The strain of the battle, the feverish chill, and the sheer, suffocating indignation boiling in his chest collided all at once; the harder he fought to stand, the more his body gave out. Under the violent surge of emotion, his throat hitched—and he actually coughed up a thick mouthful of dark blood onto the stone.

The moment the dark pool splattered the ground, Wei Wuxian’s clownish grin vanished. Dropping into an instant crouch, his fingers struck several acupoints across Lan Wangji’s chest in rapid succession. "There we go! Stagnant blood cleared. No need to thank me!"

The instant that mouthful of black, congealed blood cleared his throat, the suffocating, leaden tightness crushing Lan Wangji’s chest eased dramatically. Piecing together the sequence of events, understanding finally dawned on him.

From the moment they’d set foot on Mount Muxi, Wei Wuxian had noticed how grim and pale Lan Wangji looked. Suspecting he had dark, uncirculated blood pooled in his core from internal injuries, he had staged this brazen little performance purely to shock him into coughing it up.

Even knowing the motive was born of pure goodwill, a dark flush of embarrassment and indignation still colored Lan Wangji’s ears. "...Must you resort to such grotesque antics?!"

"Keeping that stale blood trapped in your chest would’ve ruined your core," Wei Wuxian reasoned breezily. "One good scare, and out it pops! Relax, I’m not into men—I’m not about to take advantage of you in the dark."

Lan Wangji clipped out, "Ridiculous!"

Wei Wuxian had long since clocked that Lan Wangji’s fuse was shorter than a burnt wick today. Waving an airy hand, he gave in without a fight. "Fine, fine. I’m ridiculous. Ridiculous to the bone, absolute king of nonsense."

As he spoke, a bone-deep subterranean draft snaked up his bare spine, sending a violent shiver through his frame. He bounded up to gather an armful of dead twigs and brittle brush, setting them in a pile before flicking a newly drawn fire talisman from his palm.

The dry kindling caught with a crackle, tossing sparks into the dark. Wei Wuxian mashed the selected herbs into a coarse paste between his palms, slit open the hem of Lan Wangji’s trousers, and spread the green mash evenly across the three ragged, sluggishly bleeding puncture wounds on his leg.

Suddenly, a pale hand clamped around his wrist, halting his fingers mid-motion.

Wei Wuxian blinked. "What?"

Without uttering a word, Lan Wangji scooped a generous portion of the crushed herbs straight out of Wei Wuxian’s palm and slammed it flat over Wei Wuxian’s bare chest.

The sudden contact sent a blinding jolt of agony through Wei Wuxian’s nerves, pulling a strangled shriek from his throat: "Aagh!"

In the chaos, he’d completely forgotten the fresh, raw iron brand scorched into his own flesh—still weeping blood, and soaked through with stagnant lake water.

Lan Wangji pulled his hand back, watching in silence as Wei Wuxian sucked in ragged, hissing breaths of air through clenched teeth. Grimacing, Wei Wuxian painstakingly peeled the medicinal paste from his chest bit by bit and slapped it back onto Lan Wangji’s mangled shin.

"Don't be so generous," Wei Wuxian huffed through the pain. "I get scraped up all the time. Back at Lotus Pier, I dive into the lake with fresh cuts every summer—I'm used to it. There's only so much herb in one little pouch, barely enough for one of us. Your three gaping puncture holes need it a hell of a lot more than—ow!"

Lan Wangji’s face remained dark as a storm cloud. After a long beat, his voice dropped, quiet and stern: "If you know how much it hurts, perhaps you will think twice before acting so recklessly next time."

Wei Wuxian groaned, "Did I have a choice? You think I wanted to take a red-hot iron to the ribs? Who could've guessed that Wang Lingjiao was that twisted—aiming straight for the poor girl's eyes! Mianmian is a young maiden, and a pretty one at that. If she lost an eye or walked around with a brand burned into her cheek for the rest of her days, how tragic would that be?"

Lan Wangji’s tone was clipped, running cold. "The mark burned into your chest will never fade either."

"That's completely different," Wei Wuxian shot back. "It’s not on my face, is it? Besides, I’m a man! What’s there to be afraid of? What kind of man walks through life without picking up a few scars along the way?"

Bare-chested, he squatted by the blaze, prodding the kindling with a dry stick to coax the flames higher. "Look at it from another angle: sure, this mark is permanent, but it means I took a hit to protect a girl. And mark my words, that girl is going to remember me for the rest of her life! She won't ever forget me, not in this lifetime. When you really think about it, it's actually pretty—"

A violent shove caught him squarely by the shoulder, shoving him back as Lan Wangji’s voice cracked in a sudden, furious roar:

"So you know! You know damn well she will never forget you for the rest of her life!!!"

The shove landed right against the fresh burn on his chest. Clutching his ribs, Wei Wuxian tumbled backward onto the hard dirt, letting out an agonized yelp: "...Lan Zhan!"

Sprawled flat on the cold ground, cold sweat drenched his brow from the sheer blinding pain. Straining his neck upward, he groaned, "...Lan Zhan, you... What did I ever do to you?! Did I murder your father in a past life or something?!"

Lan Wangji’s fists clenched white-knuckled at his sides.

After a tense second, his fingers slowly loosened, and he moved to push himself up to help Wei Wuxian. But Wei Wuxian was already scrambling backward like a frightened crab, his hand held up defensively. "Alright, alright! I get it, you despise me! I'll sit over here, fine?! Don't come any closer! Don't shove me again—it hurts like hell!"

The burn sat on his left flank; every time he lifted his left arm, the skin pulled with a searing sting. Tucking himself away on the far side of the fire, Wei Wuxian scooped up the strips of torn white fabric, using his right hand to fling them across the gap so they landed near Lan Wangji’s boots. "Bandage it yourself. I'm staying right here."

He draped his soaked outer robe over a nearby stone, letting the heat of the flames bake it dry.

They sat in thick, heavy silence for an eternity before Wei Wuxian couldn't bear the quiet any longer. "Lan Zhan, you're really acting bizarre today. So rough, and barking at me like that—it doesn't sound like you at all."

Lan Wangji's jaw was tight. "If you harbor no genuine intentions, do not flirt with others so carelessly! You act entirely on whim, yet you leave everyone around you in absolute turmoil!"

Wei Wuxian blinked in confusion. "I wasn't flirting with you, was I? If anyone's in turmoil, it shouldn't be you. Unless..."

Lan Wangji’s tone turned sharp as a blade. "Unless what?"

Wei Wuxian’s eyes danced with sudden mischief. "Unless... Lan Zhan, you have a crush on Mianmian!"

A heavy pause settled over the rocks before Lan Wangji ground out, freezing and rigid, "Cease your nonsense."

Wei Wuxian grinned, "Fine, then I'll talk sense instead."

"Do you truly find joy in this endless, petty squabbling?"

"Endless joy! And for the record, it's not just my tongue that's quick—I'm fast on my feet, too."

"..." Lan Wangji looked down, muttering under his breath, "Why do I even waste my breath talking to you..."

Before he even realized what he was doing, Wei Wuxian had already drifted back across the dirt, sitting right beside him again, entirely oblivious to the danger. "Because you're stuck with me! We're the only two unlucky bastards left down here. If you don't talk to me, who else are you going to talk to?"

Lan Wangji cast a dark, brooding glance at the shameless pest beside him. Just as Wei Wuxian was winding up to flash him another cheeky smirk, Lan Wangji suddenly leaned down.

Wei Wuxian’s world exploded into pure, unadulterated terror:

"Aaaaagh! Stop it! Let go! Stop, stop, STOP!!!"

Lan Wangji had buried his face into the crook of Wei Wuxian’s arm, sinking his teeth clean through the flesh with vicious, uncompromising force. Hearing the frantic shrieking, he didn't ease up in the slightest—if anything, his jaw clamped down harder!

Wei Wuxian flailed wildly: "Are you letting go or not?! Let go or I'll kick you! Don't think I won't kick a cripple, I swear to the gods I will!!!"

"Stop biting! Stop biting! I'll leave! I'm leaving! I'll get out of your hair, just let go and I'm gone!!!"

"Lan Zhan, you've completely lost your mind! You're a dog! You're an actual dog! LET GO!!!"

By the time Lan Wangji finally had his fill of vengeance and unhinged his jaw, Wei Wuxian scrambled backward in a frantic, uncoordinated tumble, practically throwing himself against the far wall of the cavern. "Don't you come near me!"

Lan Wangji slowly straightened his spine. With meticulous, unhurried grace, he smoothed his rumpled robes and brushed a stray lock of hair behind his ear, his lashes cast downward in serene, undisturbed silence—acting for all the world as if the unhinged brawler who had just shoved, cursed, and bitten someone had nothing whatsoever to do with him.

Nursing the bloody ring of teeth marks indented deep into his forearm, Wei Wuxian squatted by the fire in lingering shock, poking the embers with a stick while his mind spun in dizzy circles: What is this guy's problem?! Sure, he pushed me out of the way of the beast, but I literally hauled him out of its jaws! I'm not asking for a grand debt of gratitude or anything, but after going through hell together, can't we at least be friendly? Am I... am I really as insufferable as Jiang Cheng says I am?!

Right in the middle of his existential crisis, Lan Wangji’s voice cut through the quiet:

"Thank you."

Wei Wuxian blinked, thinking his ears were playing tricks on him. Looking up, Lan Wangji was looking directly at him, his expression deeply solemn as he repeated, "Thank you."

Seeing him lower his head in what looked like the start of a formal bow, Wei Wuxian panicked, twisting his torso away: "Stop, stop, none of that! I’ve got a terrible allergy to people thanking me, especially when someone like you delivers it with such grave, stone-faced reverence. It's giving me goosebumps! And definitely don't bow to me."

Lan Wangji’s expression remained flat as water. "You are overthinking. Even if I wished to bow, I cannot move."

Seeing him finally settle back into his usual, dry self—and actually hearing two genuine 'thank you's fall from his lips—Wei Wuxian’s mood brightened instantly. His natural inclination to crowd into people's personal space flared up, and he nearly shuffled back over to Lan Wangji's side before a phantom throb from the fresh bite mark on his arm reminded him that the man had gone feral barely five minutes ago. Who knew when the next wave would hit?

Reining himself in, he stared up at the pitch-black cavern ceiling, turning serious: "Jiang Cheng and the others made it out. It'll take them a day or two to hike down the mountain, and once they hit the bottom, they'll head straight for their own sects—nobody is stupid enough to report back to the Wen Clan. But with their swords confiscated, who knows how long it'll take them to rally a rescue party. We're probably stuck down here for quite a while. We need to figure out a plan."

He paused, adding, "The silver lining is that the monster is holed up in the black pool and hasn't chased us into the tunnels. But the flip side is that it's refusing to budge, sitting right on top of the underwater exit so we can't leave either."

Lan Wangji said, "It may not be a mere monster. Look at its form—what does it resemble?"

Wei Wuxian blurted out, "A giant bastard of a turtle!"

"A sacred beast shares that exact form."

Wei Wuxian’s brow raised. "The divine beast Xuanwu?"

The Xuanwu—also known as the Dark Warrior—was a divine union of turtle and serpent, an ancient water deity ruling over the northern seas and the underworld realms.

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod.

Wei Wuxian bared his teeth in mock ferocity. "A divine beast that looks like that? Packed with fangs, ravenous for human flesh? That's a far cry from the legends, don't you think?"

"It is, of course, no true divine beast," Lan Wangji explained. "Rather, it is a failed attempt at ascension—a warped, corrupted entity. A deformed counterfeit of the true Xuanwu."

"Deformed?"

"I once read an account in an ancient text," Lan Wangji said. "Four hundred years ago, a 'False Xuanwu' terrorized the lands of Qishan. It grew to monstrous proportions, devouring living humans by the thousands. Cultivators of that era dubbed it the 'Xuanwu of Slaughter'."

Wei Wuxian’s eyes widened. "So the beast Wen Chao dragged us out to hunt is this four-hundred-year-old Xuanwu of Slaughter?"

"It is far larger than the ancient texts described, but it matches the records."

Wei Wuxian rubbed his chin. "Well, four centuries is plenty of time to pack on the pounds. Was it never put down back then?"

"No," Lan Wangji replied. "A coalition of cultivators formed an alliance to slay it, but that winter brought an unprecedented blizzard of bitter cold. The Xuanwu of Slaughter vanished into the frozen wilds, never to be seen again."

Wei Wuxian nodded slowly. "Hibernated, then."
